clue.text: No obstacles in this course that. Alfred's about to follow

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the short name round so it reads from the other end

parts.note: Alf is the familiar short form of the name Alfred
to follow a trail is to trace it

explanation.surface: A man named Alfred is about to try a course with no jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ALF (short for Alfred) into FLA, which is followed by TRACE. A flat race is a horse race run without hurdles or fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A race on the flat is run over a course with no hurdles or fences to jump.

clue.text: Pass the ball to a defender, getting a whistle

parts.note: in football to feed a player is to pass the ball to him
a back is a defensive player in football

explanation.surface: A player passes to a defender and the referee blows his whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whistle' is the shriek from a loudspeaker, not a referee's whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: The howl when a microphone picks up its own loudspeaker is called this, a shrill whistle.

clue.text: Study of man loses what rope it has for collective work

indicators.note: loses means letters are taken away from the subject's name

parts.note: anthropology is the study of humankind
the subject's name contains the letters R, O, P of rope, without the E

explanation.surface: The study of man loses its rope and turns into collective work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what rope it has' is precise: the subject's name holds R, O, P but no E, and 'loses' strips just those three.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthology is a collection of pieces by various writers, so a collective work.

explanation.surface: The page was strictly governed by lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governs, so ruled means controlled; ruled paper is marked with straight lines.

indicators.note: in means the word for man is put inside the other word

parts.note: a clot is a fool; the 's gives the plural-looking S
he can stand for a man

explanation.surface: A man is dressed in a jester's costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. Clot is British slang for a fool, and the 's supplies the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old word for garments, so a synonym.

clue.text: Eight days a month on the road

parts.note: Oct. is the abbreviation for the month October
Ave. is the abbreviation for avenue, a kind of road

explanation.surface: Someone spends a week and a day, or a whole month, travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church calendar an octave is the eight-day period that begins with a feast day.
explanation.definitionFit: In church usage the eight-day festival period starting on a feast is called by this name.

parts.note: a motor is a car
a race of people is a nation

explanation.surface: Someone goes red after a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' means a people, not a contest. Carnation is a pink colour, so 'Blush' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnation is a pinkish-red shade, like the colour of a blush.

parts.note: a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: Sadly there is a shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an old cry of regret, like alas: a synonym.

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
her refers to a lady

explanation.surface: Someone ties up a lady too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TIE into EIT, followed by HER. 'Tie up' looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Used at the end of a negative ('nor can I either'), the word adds a point, like besides.

indicators.note: twice says the reversed letters are written two times
up in a down clue means these letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone flies up East Street twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns E + ST into TSE, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that carries sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Last of the forty about to crack up

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the word that follows it
about means the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: The fortieth person is near to breaking down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack up' means praise highly, not have a breakdown; 'about' wraps forty round 'to' and 'Last of' takes the final letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack something up is an informal way to praise it highly.

indicators.note: careless suggests the letters are thrown together without order, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: Braves who are careless are not keeping a lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careless' tells you to rearrange the letters of BRAVES and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and watchful means noticing things carefully: a synonym.

parts.note: blood is a bodily fluid; the 's gives the S
hot is a stronger word for warm

explanation.surface: Blood is warm and red in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Fluid's' gives an S, so BLOOD + S + HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are said to be bloodshot when their whites look red with swollen veins.

clue.text: A deer's back leg, in part

parts.note: a and an are two forms of the same article

indicators.note: back tells us the animal's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: an elk is a large deer; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Someone describes part of a deer's hind leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A deer' reads as 'an elk', and 'back' turns only the animal. 'back leg' looks like the definition, but 'back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint between foot and shin is one part of the leg.

indicators.note: a mixture of letters means they are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A very rich person stirs a sugary mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' says to rearrange SUCROSE. Croesus was a king of ancient Lydia famed for his wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus, king of Lydia, became a byword for a man of enormous wealth.

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a fell is an animal's hide or skin
flint is a hard stone

explanation.surface: Scrooge trips over a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' is a noun meaning skin, not the past of fall. Scrooge is Dickens's miser.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge, Dickens's miser, is the type of a stingy person.

clue.text: Wait around, the French are not poisonous

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for wait the other way round

parts.note: to bide is to wait
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone waiting nearby is told the French food is safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the reversal of the word for wait; 'Wait around' looks like loitering.
explanation.definitionFit: Something safe to eat is fit for the table, so not poisonous.

clue.text: Rely on a GI to turn into a soldier

indicators.note: to turn into means these letters change into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Count on an American GI to become a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn into' says to rearrange RELY ON A GI.
explanation.definitionFit: A legionary was a foot soldier in a Roman legion.

clue.text: He would come down without a cape

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first piece goes around the letter

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he would
to land is to come down

explanation.surface: A man would descend without wearing a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. 'cape' is a promontory, not a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a point of land jutting into the sea, a promontory.

clue.text: Numberless dairymen include it in their returns

indicators.note: in their returns tells us the letters run backwards inside that word
include it says the needed letters are tucked inside the word dairymen

explanation.surface: Countless dairymen add this to their tax returns.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'dairymen' from right to left and the answer is in it. 'returns' sounds like tax forms but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A myriad is a countless host, so as an adjective it means innumerable.

explanation.surface: Someone pays to have the edges trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as DE-FRAY: removing the frayed edges. The question mark flags the made-up sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay them; whimsically, removing frayed threads tidies the edges.

indicators.note: back tells us the hero's first name is written from end to start

parts.note: Eugene Onegin is Pushkin's verse-novel hero, so Onegin stands for his first name Eugene

explanation.surface: Onegin is told to go back, right back.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene Onegin is the hero of Pushkin's verse novel, so 'Onegin' supplies his first name, which 'back' turns. The first 'back' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue (more often spelt renege) is to go back on a promise.

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the cross-referenced word
up in a down clue means the word for always is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ever means always
the answer to 25 across is a synonym of lie

explanation.surface: Ease up, always, about the number 25.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for always and 'about' wraps it round the 25-across synonym; 'Ease up' looks like the definition but 'up' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain is to lessen or soothe it: a synonym.

indicators.note: different means the letters take a different order

explanation.surface: A companion comes from a different sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' says to rearrange SECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort accompanies someone, so is a companion.

explanation.surface: Someone puts out some snuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff a candle is to extinguish it; snuff is also finely ground tobacco for sniffing.

clue.text: Join central part of up train

annotationWithheld.why: Join central part of up train (5): the answer UNITE has no parse from these words (the scan prints the same text), and no source gives the setter's reading
annotationWithheld.clue: Join central part of up train

indicators.note: a version is a new rendering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A false account fools the head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' says to rearrange FOOLS and HEAD. 'Lying' here is the noun, the act of telling lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling lies is the same act as uttering an untruth, a synonym.

clue.text: Such days occur in several months

definitions.text: Such days occur in several months

parts.words: Such days occur in several months
parts.note: the Church's quarterly fasting days share a name with the closing five letters of three month names late in the year

explanation.surface: Certain special days fall in several months.
explanation.definitionFit: Ember days are the Church's quarterly fasts, and three month names late in the year end in these letters.

clue.text: Begin to speak after swallowing one drink

indicators.note: after swallowing means the word for speak takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone starts talking after downing a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after swallowing' signals the container; 'Begin to speak' looks like one phrase, but only 'Begin' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to start or come into being: a synonym.

clue.text: African master or bachelor of arts, faint-hearted

indicators.note: hearted means placed at the heart of the degree letters

parts.note: wan means pale and faint

explanation.surface: Is the African master a timid arts graduate?
explanation.walkthrough: 'faint-hearted' reads as WAN put at the heart of BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bwana is a Swahili form of address meaning sir or boss.

clue.text: Go outside to dine, by agreement

indicators.note: outside means the word for go is placed around the word for dine

parts.note: a go at something is a try
to eat is to dine

explanation.surface: Two parties agree to go out to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' signals the container; 'Go' is the noun sense, as in 'have a go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

parts.note: Bet is a short form of the name Elizabeth
rayed means shone with rays

explanation.surface: It was revealed that Elizabeth was glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: BET is a pet form of Elizabeth; RAYED means sent out rays.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray a secret is to reveal it, so disclosed is a synonym.
